vulnerabilities.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
vulnerabilities.explanation: The function 'save_note' reads an unbounded note and allocates a backup buffer based on its length without verifying the size.
The function 'save_note' copies the full note into a fixed-size backup buffer and then prints the note directly without bounds checks.
The function 'save_note' frees the same allocation for backup twice, causing a double free.

vulnerabilities.cwe_name: Buffer Access Using Size of Source Buffer
vulnerabilities.explanation: The code uses strlen() or a source-sized expression to drive a destination write instead of using a destination-sized expression.
The code passes externally controlled text directly as the format argument to printf or a similar function.
The code accepts unvalidated text and uses it in a destination buffer without validating that it will fit.
The code frees the same allocation through more than one cleanup path.
The code uses gets(), sprintf(), or another unsafe C standard function instead of a safer alternative.
